## AI Code Review Agent Architecture: Cross-Tool Research Report

### 1. CODERABBIT

**Architecture:** Multi-agent pipeline with 5 specialized agents (Review, Verification, Chat, Pre-Merge Checks, Finishing Touches). Each review runs in an isolated Google Cloud Run container (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM). Two-layer sandboxing: Cloud Run gen2 microVM + Jailkit process isolation inside the container. 50+ deterministic static analysis tools (Semgrep, ESLint, Ruff, TruffleHog, etc.) run alongside the LLM review -- the AI review is augmented by, not a replacement for, traditional linting/SAST.

**Prompting:** System prompts not published. Customization via `.coderabbit.yaml` with `profile: "assertive"` vs `"chill"`, per-path instructions (up to 20K chars per glob pattern), and tone instructions. "Living Memory" system learns from accepted/dismissed comments per org. No few-shot examples or chain-of-thought scaffolding exposed.

**Output:** Four severity tiers: Critical / High / Medium / Low. Five analysis categories: security, quality, performance, best practices, bugs. Inline comments with suggested fixes (one-click apply). PR walkthrough with sequence diagrams and review effort estimates. No confidence scores exposed publicly.

**Integration:** GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket (only tool on all four). **Can block merges** when `request_changes_workflow: true` + checks in error mode -- submits a GitHub "Request Changes" review. Auto-approves when issues resolved. Override via "Ignore failed checks" checkbox.

**Models:** Multi-model routing. Stage 1 (context gathering): NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 30B (1M context, fast). Stage 2 (deep review): OpenAI o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2-Codex + Anthropic Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.5. Rate-limited via FluxNinja Aperture with weighted fair queuing (~40K tokens/min for GPT-4 class).

**Sources:** [CodeRabbit Architecture Docs](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/overview/architecture), [Google Cloud Run case study](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/how-coderabbit-built-its-ai-code-review-agent-with-google-cloud-run), [OpenAI blog on CodeRabbit](https://openai.com/index/coderabbit/)

---

### 2. GITHUB COPILOT

**Architecture:** Redesigned March 2026 to agentic architecture. The review agent uses tool-calling to read related files, inspect directory structure, trace cross-file dependencies, and read linked issues/PRs before generating comments. **Strictly read-only** -- never modifies code. "Implement suggestion" hands off to a separate coding agent running in ephemeral GitHub Actions. No shared state between review and coding agents. Runs on GitHub Actions infrastructure.

**Prompting:** System prompt not disclosed. Customizable via `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (repo-wide) and `.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md` (path-specific). MCP server integration available. Review effort levels: Low (default) and Medium (deeper analysis, more compute).

**Output:** Inline comments on logical multi-line ranges. Severity labels (shipped May 2026): High / Medium / Low. Similar/recurring issues grouped with batch autofix. No confidence scores exposed. Always posts as "Comment" review -- never "Approve" or "Request changes." Silent in 29% of reviews (averages 5.1 comments when it does comment).

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory only -- does not count toward required approvals. Automatic or manual trigger via Reviewers menu. Optional "Review new pushes" for re-review on each commit. CodeQL/ESLint/PMD findings can be integrated via SARIF.

**Models:** GitHub says "tuned model mix" -- deliberately opaque. Third-party analysis suggests GPT-4 premium with GPT-4.1 fallback. Accepted 16% latency increase for 6% quality improvement with the agentic redesign. No public temperature or configuration info.

**Scale:** 60M+ reviews performed, 20% of all GitHub code reviews, 12K+ orgs on automatic review.

**Sources:** [GitHub Blog: Agentic Architecture](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-03-05-copilot-code-review-now-runs-on-an-agentic-architecture/), [GitHub Docs: Copilot Code Review](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/use-copilot-agents/copilot-code-review), [60M Reviews Blog Post](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/60-million-copilot-code-reviews-and-counting/)

---

### 3. CURSOR (BugBot)

**Architecture:** Rebuilt from pipeline (V1) to fully agentic (V2) in fall 2025. V1 used 8 parallel LLM passes with randomized diff ordering + majority voting (>=2/8 passes must flag an issue) + category filtering + validator model. V2 is a single agent with dynamic tool-calling: `read_file`, `list_directory`, `find_references`, `search_codebase`, `check_dependencies`, `get_commit_history`. Self-determines investigation depth (2-3 tool calls for simple PRs, 10+ for complex). Custom Rust-based Git layer handles 2M+ PRs/month at scale.

**Prompting:** V1 used restrained prompting to minimize false positives. V2 reversed this -- **aggressive prompting** encourages investigating every suspicious pattern; false positive reduction handled by iterative tool-based verification. Security review prompt (analyzed by Snyk): 15 lines total, four-step methodology, explicit constraint against pushing changes. Custom rules via `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`.

**Output:** Structured data model with: file path, line range, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), category (Logic/Security/Perf/Edge Case), title, explanation, suggested fix, confidence float, resolution status. Three remediation buttons: "Fix in Cursor," "Fix in Web," "Autofix."

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory PR comments. `/review` command (Cursor 3.7+) runs locally before push. `cursor-cli review` available for CI/CD. BugBot Autofix spawns Cloud Agents; 35%+ of proposed changes merged without modification. Resolution rate: 70-79% (up from 52% at launch).

**Models:** "Combination of frontier and in-house models" -- not disclosed. Security review dedup uses Gemini Flash 2.5. Composer 2.5 (generation) built on Kimi K2.5 but not used for BugBot. Self-improving: continuous learning from 110K+ repos, 44K+ learned rules.

**Sources:** [Cursor BugBot](https://cursor.com/bugbot), [Building a Better BugBot](https://cursor.com/blog/building-bugbot), [BugBot Self-Improves](https://cursor.com/blog/bugbot-learning), [Snyk analysis of Cursor security prompts](https://snyk.io/blog/cursor-security-agent-prompts/)

---

### 4. WINDSURF (formerly Codeium)

**Architecture:** After Cognition acquired Codeium (Dec 2025, ~$250M), review is handled by **Devin Review** as a cloud service, separate from the local Cascade IDE agent. Review does not share a session or context window with code generation. Triggered automatically when a PR is marked "ready for review" or manually via `@windsurf /review`.

**Output/Integration:** Posts GitHub review comments inline on the diff. Edits PR titles and descriptions. No documented severity taxonomy or structured output schema. **Does NOT block merges.** GitHub Cloud only, Teams/Enterprise plans, 50 files/PR limit, 500 reviews/month org-wide rate limit. Configuration through Windsurf dashboard (no TOML/YAML config file).

**Models:** Not disclosed for the review surface. Supports Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, and SWE-1.5/SWE-1.6 across the IDE.

**Sources:** [Windsurf PR Reviews Docs](https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/windsurf-reviews/windsurf-reviews), [Windsurf 2.0 Review](https://chatforest.com/reviews/windsurf-2-0-cognition-devin-agent-command-center-ide-review/)

---

### 5. OPENCODE (+ Cloudflare's Production System)

**Architecture (OpenCode native):** Review is a built-in agent mode isolated via YAML permission gating: `edit: deny`, `bash: deny` makes it read-only. Runs as a `subagent` spawned by the orchestrator. Minimal system prompt: "Focus on: code quality, potential bugs, edge cases, performance, security. Provide constructive feedback without making direct changes."

**Architecture (Cloudflare's production system, built on OpenCode):** The most sophisticated implementation found. A **Coordinator agent** spawns up to **7 specialized sub-reviewers** in parallel: Code Quality, Security, Performance, Documentation, Release Management, Compliance, AGENTS.md Reviewer. Risk tiering before dispatch: Trivial (<=10 lines, 2 agents, ~$0.20), Lite (<=100 lines, 4 agents, ~$0.67), Full (>100 lines or security paths, 7+ agents, ~$1.68). Security-sensitive file paths always trigger full review. 131K review runs across 48K MRs in the first 30 days.

**Output (Cloudflare):** Structured XML with three severity tiers: Critical (causes outage/exploitable), Warning (measurable regression), Suggestion (improvement). **Critical findings block merge** via GitLab `requested_changes`. "Break glass" escape hatch (0.6% usage rate). Re-review on new commits is delta-aware -- reads developer disagreement replies and adjudicates.

**Models (Cloudflare):** Three tiers: Top (Coordinator: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.4), Standard (heavy lifting: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.3 Codex), Lightweight (docs: Kimi K2.5). Dynamically overridable via Cloudflare Worker + Workers KV. Circuit breaker per tier with failback chains.

**Sources:** [OpenCode Agents Docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/), [Cloudflare Blog: AI Code Review](https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-code-review/), [Martin Alderson: OpenCode in CI/CD](https://martinalderson.com/posts/using-opencode-in-cicd-for-ai-pull-request-reviews/)

**Also found: Spencer Marx's Open Code Review** -- multi-agent with structured discourse (AGREE/CHALLENGE/CONNECT/SURFACE moves between reviewers). 28 reviewer personas across 4 tiers including "famous engineers" (Martin Fowler, Kent Beck, Sandi Metz). Cross-reviewer debate catches false positives that single-pass misses. Source: [spencermarx/open-code-review](https://github.com/spencermarx/open-code-review)

---

### 6. OPENAI CODEX

**Architecture:** Review is the same agent engine in **read-only sandbox mode** (`--sandbox read-only`). Platform-native sandboxing: macOS Seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap, Windows Sandbox. Subagent architecture for review: documented pattern uses 3 parallel subagents -- `pr_explorer` (read-only mapping), `reviewer` (correctness/security), `docs_researcher` (API verification via MCP). Guardian AI: separate LLM judges tool calls before execution as a safety layer.

**Prompting:** Identify issues affecting correctness, performance, security, maintainability, developer experience. Flag only actionable problems introduced by the PR. `AGENTS.md` hierarchy with `## Review guidelines` sections. Closest `AGENTS.md` to each changed file takes precedence.

**Output:** Structured JSON schema enforced via `--output-schema`: `findings[]` with title (80 chars max), body, `confidence_score` (0.0-1.0), `priority` (0-3, P0=critical), `code_location` (file path + line range). Overall verdict: `"patch is correct"` / `"patch is incorrect"` with `overall_confidence_score`. Only P0 and P1 posted to GitHub.

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges** natively. GitHub Action (`openai/codex-action@v1`) posts findings as inline PR comments. Two-job CI: Codex job captures JSON, Feedback job posts comments. `@codex review` trigger on any PR. `@codex fix it` triggers cloud remediation. SDK cookbook includes GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Jenkins examples.

**Models:** gpt-5.5 recommended default ("strongest accuracy"), gpt-5.4 for reviewer subagent, gpt-5.4-mini for lightweight subagents, gpt-5.3-codex-spark for read-only exploration. `review_model` override in `config.toml`.

**Sources:** [Codex SDK Code Review Cookbook](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/build_code_review_with_codex_sdk), [Codex GitHub Integration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/integrations/github), [Codex Subagents](https://developers.openai.com/codex/subagents), [Codex Sandbox](https://developers.openai.com/codex/concepts/sandboxing)

### 7. DEVIN (Cognition)

**Architecture:** Devin Review is a **standalone product** separate from Devin's code generation (sandboxed Linux VMs). Review uses CLI mode that creates isolated git worktrees, extracts diffs using local git, executes read-only operations (file reading, grep), then sends to Devin's servers. Safety: prompt-enforced "NEVER make any commits or pushes" + pre-push Git hook. Self-review loop: generation agent self-reviews before opening PR, then Devin Review does independent second pass.

**Output:** Four-tier severity: Severe bugs / Non-severe bugs / Investigate flags / Informational flags. Diff Organization Algorithm groups changes into narrative categories and orders them sequentially. Default 3 comments per PR (customizable).

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory comments. Auto-review fires on PR open, new commits, draft-to-ready. API-triggered reviews via `POST https://api.devin.ai/v1/sessions`. **Auto-fix loop**: 70% of flagged bugs can be auto-fixed. Reads repo-level instruction files: `REVIEW.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.coderabbit.yaml`.

**Models:** SWE-1.5 / SWE-1.6 -- purpose-built RL-trained models optimized for comprehension (not generation). Frontier-size (hundreds of billions of parameters), trained end-to-end on real task environments. 950 tokens/second via Cerebras.

**Sources:** [Devin Review Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/devin-review), [Devin Review Docs](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-review), [SWE-1.5 Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/swe-1-5), [Devin Autofix Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/closing-the-agent-loop-devin-autofixes-review-comments)

### 8. SWE-AGENT / SWE-BENCH

**SWE-agent** is a fix agent, not a review agent. However, its Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) design is highly relevant: purpose-built tools with bounded output roughly double SWE-Bench scores vs raw bash. Post-edit flake8 lint with auto-revert on new errors provides a lightweight review gate.

**SWE-PRBench** (March 2026): Purpose-built code review benchmark. 350 PRs with human-annotated ground truth. Key finding: a structured 2,000-token diff-with-summary prompt **outperforms** 2,500-token full-context prompts across all 8 models tested. Frontier models detect only 15-31% of human-flagged issues.

**Adversarial Review paper** (OpenReview, June 2026): Three-agent protocol (Main + Reviewer + Critic). "Cooperative oversight is useful when disagreement is minimal, structured, and evidence-grounded." Outperforms six-agent baseline on LiveCodeBench.

**adversarial-review repo** (alecnielsen): 4-phase shell script loop using Claude + Codex cross-provider. Independent Reviews -> Cross-Review -> Meta-Review -> Synthesis. VALID/INVALID/AMBIGUOUS verdicts. Circuit breaker for stagnation. Cross-provider intentional to avoid correlated blind spots.

**"Review Beats Planning" paper** (March 2026): Dedicated post-generation review consistently outperforms elaborate upfront planning on HumanEval and EvalPlus.

**Sources:** [SWE-PRBench (arXiv 2603.26130)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26130), [Adversarial Review (OpenReview)](https://openreview.net/forum?id=fOHvpLs6zp), [adversarial-review repo](https://github.com/alecnielsen/adversarial-review), [Review Beats Planning (arXiv 2603.03406)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03406)

### 9. AMAZON CODEGURU / AMAZON Q

**Architecture:** Hybrid deterministic + LLM. CodeGuru Reviewer (sunset Nov 2025) used classical ML + program analysis (SAST taint tracking) trained on millions of Amazon internal code reviews. Amazon Q Developer replaced it with: (1) Rule-based detector library (hundreds of deterministic detectors for OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25, secrets, IaC, SCA) + (2) Generative AI via Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude Sonnet + Amazon Titan, RAG against AWS docs). Both Amazon Q and CodeGuru are being replaced by **Kiro** (Q end-of-support April 2027).

**Output:** Five CVSS-derived severity tiers: Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info, determined by a matrix of access level x effort level. Six finding categories: SAST, secrets detection, IaC issues, code quality, deployment risks, SCA. Committable code suggestions.

## AI Code Review Agent Architecture: Cross-Tool Research Report

### 1. CODERABBIT

**Architecture:** Multi-agent pipeline with 5 specialized agents (Review, Verification, Chat, Pre-Merge Checks, Finishing Touches). Each review runs in an isolated Google Cloud Run container (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM). Two-layer sandboxing: Cloud Run gen2 microVM + Jailkit process isolation inside the container. 50+ deterministic static analysis tools (Semgrep, ESLint, Ruff, TruffleHog, etc.) run alongside the LLM review -- the AI review is augmented by, not a replacement for, traditional linting/SAST.

**Prompting:** System prompts not published. Customization via `.coderabbit.yaml` with `profile: "assertive"` vs `"chill"`, per-path instructions (up to 20K chars per glob pattern), and tone instructions. "Living Memory" system learns from accepted/dismissed comments per org. No few-shot examples or chain-of-thought scaffolding exposed.

**Output:** Four severity tiers: Critical / High / Medium / Low. Five analysis categories: security, quality, performance, best practices, bugs. Inline comments with suggested fixes (one-click apply). PR walkthrough with sequence diagrams and review effort estimates. No confidence scores exposed publicly.

**Integration:** GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket (only tool on all four). **Can block merges** when `request_changes_workflow: true` + checks in error mode -- submits a GitHub "Request Changes" review. Auto-approves when issues resolved. Override via "Ignore failed checks" checkbox.

**Models:** Multi-model routing. Stage 1 (context gathering): NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 30B (1M context, fast). Stage 2 (deep review): OpenAI o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2-Codex + Anthropic Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.5. Rate-limited via FluxNinja Aperture with weighted fair queuing (~40K tokens/min for GPT-4 class).

**Sources:** [CodeRabbit Architecture Docs](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/overview/architecture), [Google Cloud Run case study](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/how-coderabbit-built-its-ai-code-review-agent-with-google-cloud-run), [OpenAI blog on CodeRabbit](https://openai.com/index/coderabbit/)

---

### 2. GITHUB COPILOT

**Architecture:** Redesigned March 2026 to agentic architecture. The review agent uses tool-calling to read related files, inspect directory structure, trace cross-file dependencies, and read linked issues/PRs before generating comments. **Strictly read-only** -- never modifies code. "Implement suggestion" hands off to a separate coding agent running in ephemeral GitHub Actions. No shared state between review and coding agents. Runs on GitHub Actions infrastructure.

**Prompting:** System prompt not disclosed. Customizable via `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (repo-wide) and `.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md` (path-specific). MCP server integration available. Review effort levels: Low (default) and Medium (deeper analysis, more compute).

**Output:** Inline comments on logical multi-line ranges. Severity labels (shipped May 2026): High / Medium / Low. Similar/recurring issues grouped with batch autofix. No confidence scores exposed. Always posts as "Comment" review -- never "Approve" or "Request changes." Silent in 29% of reviews (averages 5.1 comments when it does comment).

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory only -- does not count toward required approvals. Automatic or manual trigger via Reviewers menu. Optional "Review new pushes" for re-review on each commit. CodeQL/ESLint/PMD findings can be integrated via SARIF.

**Models:** GitHub says "tuned model mix" -- deliberately opaque. Third-party analysis suggests GPT-4 premium with GPT-4.1 fallback. Accepted 16% latency increase for 6% quality improvement with the agentic redesign. No public temperature or configuration info.

**Scale:** 60M+ reviews performed, 20% of all GitHub code reviews, 12K+ orgs on automatic review.

**Sources:** [GitHub Blog: Agentic Architecture](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-03-05-copilot-code-review-now-runs-on-an-agentic-architecture/), [GitHub Docs: Copilot Code Review](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/use-copilot-agents/copilot-code-review), [60M Reviews Blog Post](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/60-million-copilot-code-reviews-and-counting/)

---

### 3. CURSOR (BugBot)

**Architecture:** Rebuilt from pipeline (V1) to fully agentic (V2) in fall 2025. V1 used 8 parallel LLM passes with randomized diff ordering + majority voting (>=2/8 passes must flag an issue) + category filtering + validator model. V2 is a single agent with dynamic tool-calling: `read_file`, `list_directory`, `find_references`, `search_codebase`, `check_dependencies`, `get_commit_history`. Self-determines investigation depth (2-3 tool calls for simple PRs, 10+ for complex). Custom Rust-based Git layer handles 2M+ PRs/month at scale.

**Prompting:** V1 used restrained prompting to minimize false positives. V2 reversed this -- **aggressive prompting** encourages investigating every suspicious pattern; false positive reduction handled by iterative tool-based verification. Security review prompt (analyzed by Snyk): 15 lines total, four-step methodology, explicit constraint against pushing changes. Custom rules via `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`.

**Output:** Structured data model with: file path, line range, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), category (Logic/Security/Perf/Edge Case), title, explanation, suggested fix, confidence float, resolution status. Three remediation buttons: "Fix in Cursor," "Fix in Web," "Autofix."

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory PR comments. `/review` command (Cursor 3.7+) runs locally before push. `cursor-cli review` available for CI/CD. BugBot Autofix spawns Cloud Agents; 35%+ of proposed changes merged without modification. Resolution rate: 70-79% (up from 52% at launch).

**Models:** "Combination of frontier and in-house models" -- not disclosed. Security review dedup uses Gemini Flash 2.5. Composer 2.5 (generation) built on Kimi K2.5 but not used for BugBot. Self-improving: continuous learning from 110K+ repos, 44K+ learned rules.

**Sources:** [Cursor BugBot](https://cursor.com/bugbot), [Building a Better BugBot](https://cursor.com/blog/building-bugbot), [BugBot Self-Improves](https://cursor.com/blog/bugbot-learning), [Snyk analysis of Cursor security prompts](https://snyk.io/blog/cursor-security-agent-prompts/)

---

### 4. WINDSURF (formerly Codeium)

**Architecture:** After Cognition acquired Codeium (Dec 2025, ~$250M), review is handled by **Devin Review** as a cloud service, separate from the local Cascade IDE agent. Review does not share a session or context window with code generation. Triggered automatically when a PR is marked "ready for review" or manually via `@windsurf /review`.

**Output/Integration:** Posts GitHub review comments inline on the diff. Edits PR titles and descriptions. No documented severity taxonomy or structured output schema. **Does NOT block merges.** GitHub Cloud only, Teams/Enterprise plans, 50 files/PR limit, 500 reviews/month org-wide rate limit. Configuration through Windsurf dashboard (no TOML/YAML config file).

**Models:** Not disclosed for the review surface. Supports Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, and SWE-1.5/SWE-1.6 across the IDE.

**Sources:** [Windsurf PR Reviews Docs](https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/windsurf-reviews/windsurf-reviews), [Windsurf 2.0 Review](https://chatforest.com/reviews/windsurf-2-0-cognition-devin-agent-command-center-ide-review/)

### 5. OPENCODE (+ Cloudflare's Production System)

**Architecture (OpenCode native):** Review is a built-in agent mode isolated via YAML permission gating: `edit: deny`, `bash: deny` makes it read-only. Runs as a `subagent` spawned by the orchestrator. Minimal system prompt: "Focus on: code quality, potential bugs, edge cases, performance, security. Provide constructive feedback without making direct changes."

**Architecture (Cloudflare's production system, built on OpenCode):** The most sophisticated implementation found. A **Coordinator agent** spawns up to **7 specialized sub-reviewers** in parallel: Code Quality, Security, Performance, Documentation, Release Management, Compliance, AGENTS.md Reviewer. Risk tiering before dispatch: Trivial (<=10 lines, 2 agents, ~$0.20), Lite (<=100 lines, 4 agents, ~$0.67), Full (>100 lines or security paths, 7+ agents, ~$1.68). Security-sensitive file paths always trigger full review. 131K review runs across 48K MRs in the first 30 days.

**Output (Cloudflare):** Structured XML with three severity tiers: Critical (causes outage/exploitable), Warning (measurable regression), Suggestion (improvement). **Critical findings block merge** via GitLab `requested_changes`. "Break glass" escape hatch (0.6% usage rate). Re-review on new commits is delta-aware -- reads developer disagreement replies and adjudicates.

**Models (Cloudflare):** Three tiers: Top (Coordinator: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.4), Standard (heavy lifting: Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.3 Codex), Lightweight (docs: Kimi K2.5). Dynamically overridable via Cloudflare Worker + Workers KV. Circuit breaker per tier with failback chains.

**Sources:** [OpenCode Agents Docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/), [Cloudflare Blog: AI Code Review](https://blog.cloudflare.com/ai-code-review/), [Martin Alderson: OpenCode in CI/CD](https://martinalderson.com/posts/using-opencode-in-cicd-for-ai-pull-request-reviews/)

**Also found: Spencer Marx's Open Code Review** -- multi-agent with structured discourse (AGREE/CHALLENGE/CONNECT/SURFACE moves between reviewers). 28 reviewer personas across 4 tiers including "famous engineers" (Martin Fowler, Kent Beck, Sandi Metz). Cross-reviewer debate catches false positives that single-pass misses. Source: [spencermarx/open-code-review](https://github.com/spencermarx/open-code-review)

---

### 6. OPENAI CODEX

**Architecture:** Review is the same agent engine in **read-only sandbox mode** (`--sandbox read-only`). Platform-native sandboxing: macOS Seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap, Windows Sandbox. Subagent architecture for review: documented pattern uses 3 parallel subagents -- `pr_explorer` (read-only mapping), `reviewer` (correctness/security), `docs_researcher` (API verification via MCP). Guardian AI: separate LLM judges tool calls before execution as a safety layer.

**Prompting:** Identify issues affecting correctness, performance, security, maintainability, developer experience. Flag only actionable problems introduced by the PR. `AGENTS.md` hierarchy with `## Review guidelines` sections. Closest `AGENTS.md` to each changed file takes precedence.

**Output:** Structured JSON schema enforced via `--output-schema`: `findings[]` with title (80 chars max), body, `confidence_score` (0.0-1.0), `priority` (0-3, P0=critical), `code_location` (file path + line range). Overall verdict: `"patch is correct"` / `"patch is incorrect"` with `overall_confidence_score`. Only P0 and P1 posted to GitHub.

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges** natively. GitHub Action (`openai/codex-action@v1`) posts findings as inline PR comments. Two-job CI: Codex job captures JSON, Feedback job posts comments. `@codex review` trigger on any PR. `@codex fix it` triggers cloud remediation. SDK cookbook includes GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, Jenkins examples.

**Models:** gpt-5.5 recommended default ("strongest accuracy"), gpt-5.4 for reviewer subagent, gpt-5.4-mini for lightweight subagents, gpt-5.3-codex-spark for read-only exploration. `review_model` override in `config.toml`.

**Sources:** [Codex SDK Code Review Cookbook](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/build_code_review_with_codex_sdk), [Codex GitHub Integration](https://developers.openai.com/codex/integrations/github), [Codex Subagents](https://developers.openai.com/codex/subagents), [Codex Sandbox](https://developers.openai.com/codex/concepts/sandboxing)

---

### 7. DEVIN (Cognition)

**Architecture:** Devin Review is a **standalone product** separate from Devin's code generation (sandboxed Linux VMs). Review uses CLI mode that creates isolated git worktrees, extracts diffs using local git, executes read-only operations (file reading, grep), then sends to Devin's servers. Safety: prompt-enforced "NEVER make any commits or pushes" + pre-push Git hook. Self-review loop: generation agent self-reviews before opening PR, then Devin Review does independent second pass.

**Output:** Four-tier severity: Severe bugs / Non-severe bugs / Investigate flags / Informational flags. Diff Organization Algorithm groups changes into narrative categories and orders them sequentially. Default 3 comments per PR (customizable).

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory comments. Auto-review fires on PR open, new commits, draft-to-ready. API-triggered reviews via `POST https://api.devin.ai/v1/sessions`. **Auto-fix loop**: 70% of flagged bugs can be auto-fixed. Reads repo-level instruction files: `REVIEW.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.coderabbit.yaml`.

**Models:** SWE-1.5 / SWE-1.6 -- purpose-built RL-trained models optimized for comprehension (not generation). Frontier-size (hundreds of billions of parameters), trained end-to-end on real task environments. 950 tokens/second via Cerebras.

**Sources:** [Devin Review Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/devin-review), [Devin Review Docs](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-review), [SWE-1.5 Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/swe-1-5), [Devin Autofix Blog](https://cognition.ai/blog/closing-the-agent-loop-devin-autofixes-review-comments)

---

### 8. SWE-AGENT / SWE-BENCH

**SWE-agent** is a fix agent, not a review agent. However, its Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) design is highly relevant: purpose-built tools with bounded output roughly double SWE-Bench scores vs raw bash. Post-edit flake8 lint with auto-revert on new errors provides a lightweight review gate.

**SWE-PRBench** (March 2026): Purpose-built code review benchmark. 350 PRs with human-annotated ground truth. Key finding: a structured 2,000-token diff-with-summary prompt **outperforms** 2,500-token full-context prompts across all 8 models tested. Frontier models detect only 15-31% of human-flagged issues.

**Adversarial Review paper** (OpenReview, June 2026): Three-agent protocol (Main + Reviewer + Critic). "Cooperative oversight is useful when disagreement is minimal, structured, and evidence-grounded." Outperforms six-agent baseline on LiveCodeBench.

**adversarial-review repo** (alecnielsen): 4-phase shell script loop using Claude + Codex cross-provider. Independent Reviews -> Cross-Review -> Meta-Review -> Synthesis. VALID/INVALID/AMBIGUOUS verdicts. Circuit breaker for stagnation. Cross-provider intentional to avoid correlated blind spots.

**"Review Beats Planning" paper** (March 2026): Dedicated post-generation review consistently outperforms elaborate upfront planning on HumanEval and EvalPlus.

**Sources:** [SWE-PRBench (arXiv 2603.26130)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26130), [Adversarial Review (OpenReview)](https://openreview.net/forum?id=fOHvpLs6zp), [adversarial-review repo](https://github.com/alecnielsen/adversarial-review), [Review Beats Planning (arXiv 2603.03406)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03406)

---

### 9. AMAZON CODEGURU / AMAZON Q

**Architecture:** Hybrid deterministic + LLM. CodeGuru Reviewer (sunset Nov 2025) used classical ML + program analysis (SAST taint tracking) trained on millions of Amazon internal code reviews. Amazon Q Developer replaced it with: (1) Rule-based detector library (hundreds of deterministic detectors for OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25, secrets, IaC, SCA) + (2) Generative AI via Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude Sonnet + Amazon Titan, RAG against AWS docs). Both Amazon Q and CodeGuru are being replaced by **Kiro** (Q end-of-support April 2027).

**Output:** Five CVSS-derived severity tiers: Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info, determined by a matrix of access level x effort level. Six finding categories: SAST, secrets detection, IaC issues, code quality, deployment risks, SCA. Committable code suggestions.

**Integration:** **Does NOT block merges.** Advisory. GitHub App via Marketplace, auto-review on PR creation (not subsequent commits), `/q review` for manual trigger, `/q <question>` for interactive Q&A about findings. Custom rules via `.amazonq/rules/` in Markdown.

**Models:** Anthropic Claude Sonnet + Amazon Titan via Bedrock, routed per task. Rule-based detectors are not LLM-powered. Fine-tuned on 20+ years of AWS best practices.

**Sources:** [Amazon Q Code Reviews (AWS Docs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/code-reviews.html), [Code Issue Severity (AWS Docs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/code-issue-severity.html), [Interactive Code Review (AWS Blog)](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/introducing-an-interactive-code-review-experience-with-amazon-q-developer-in-github/)

---

### 10. QODO AI (formerly CodiumAI / PR-Agent)

**Architecture:** Open-source PR-Agent uses single LLM call per tool (~30 seconds). Four-layer architecture: UI -> Orchestration (`PRAgent` class routing slash commands) -> Specialized Tools (`PRReviewer`, `PRDescription`, `PRCodeSuggestions`) -> Platform Abstraction (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps/Gitea). Qodo Merge 2.0 (commercial, Feb 2026) adds multi-agent ensemble: Bug Detection + Security Analysis + Code Quality + Test Coverage agents, coordinated by a Judge Agent that deduplicates and filters, plus a Recommendation Agent using PR history.

**Prompting:** Most transparent of any tool. From `pr_reviewer_prompts.toml`: role framing, scope constraints (new code only, no pre-existing issues), calibrated confidence asymmetry (high-severity flagged even at lower confidence with uncertainty noted; low-severity requires high confidence). Anti-noise: "precision over comprehensiveness, preferring omission to unfounded speculation." Teaches the model the diff format explicitly.

**Output:** Structured YAML with: `key_issues_to_review` (file path, issue header, content, line range), `security_concerns`, `relevant_tests`, `estimated_effort_to_review_[1-5]`, optional `score` (0-100), `can_be_split` (SubPR decomposition), `ticket_compliance`. Auto-generated labels: `"possible security issue"`, `"review effort [x/5]"`. Allow/Warn/Block decision model. `num_max_findings = 3` caps noise.

**Integration:** Does not natively block merges but labels enable CI gating. `persistent_comment = true` updates same comment on re-runs. GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea. CLI, GitHub Action, Docker, polling server. `/implement` command generates fix code from review findings.

**Models:** Default: `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23`, fallback: `gpt-5.4-mini`. **Temperature: 0.2** (deliberate low for deterministic review). Reasoning effort: `"medium"`. LiteLLM handler supports any provider. Per-command model overrides supported. Commercial version: credit system (Opus costs 5 credits, standard costs 1).

**Benchmark:** F1 60.1% (highest among 8 competing tools), recall 56.7%, ~25% false positive rate.

**Sources:** [PR-Agent GitHub](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent), [Qodo 2.0 Blog](https://www.qodo.ai/blog/introducing-qodo-2-0-agentic-code-review/), [PR-Agent Reviewer Prompts TOML](https://github.com/qodo-ai/pr-agent/blob/main/pr_agent/settings/pr_reviewer_prompts.toml), [Augment Code: How we built a high-quality AI code review agent](https://www.augmentcode.com/blog/how-we-built-high-quality-ai-code-review-agent)

---

## CROSS-CUTTING PATTERNS

### Isolation Strategies (ranked by rigor)
1. **Sandbox enforcement** (Codex read-only sandbox, CodeRabbit Jailkit containers) -- physically cannot write
2. **Permission gating** (OpenCode `edit: deny, bash: deny`) -- agent config prevents writes
3. **Separate system** (Devin Review, Copilot, Cursor BugBot) -- different codebase/service entirely
4. **Prompt-only** ("do not make changes") -- weakest, relies on model compliance

### Output Structure Patterns
| Tool | Severity Tiers | Confidence Score | Structured Format |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| CodeRabbit | 4 (Critical/High/Medium/Low) | No | Inline comments |
| Copilot | 3 (High/Medium/Low) | No | Inline comments |
| Cursor BugBot | 4 (Critical/High/Medium/Low) | Yes (float) | Structured data model |
| Codex | 4 (P0-P3) | Yes (0.0-1.0) | Enforced JSON schema |
| Devin | 4 (Severe/Non-severe/Investigate/Info) | No | PR comments |
| Qodo | 3 (Allow/Warn/Block) + effort 1-5 | No (calibrated language) | Structured YAML |
| Amazon Q | 5 (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) | No | Inline comments |
| Cloudflare | 3 (Critical/Warning/Suggestion) | No | Structured XML |

### Merge Blocking
Only **two** tools can actually block merges: **CodeRabbit** (via GitHub "Request Changes" review) and **Cloudflare's system** (via GitLab `requested_changes`). All others are advisory only.

### Model Strategy Patterns
1. **Single model** (Copilot, Devin) -- simplest, one model does everything
2. **Tiered by role** (Cloudflare: Opus for coordinator, Sonnet for reviewers, Kimi for docs; Codex: gpt-5.5 for reviewer, gpt-5.4-mini for explorer)
3. **Multi-model routing** (CodeRabbit: Nemotron for context, o3/Claude for review)
4. **Cross-provider** (adversarial-review: Claude + Codex intentionally to avoid correlated blind spots)

### Key Research Findings
- **Review beats planning**: dedicated post-generation review outperforms elaborate upfront planning (arXiv 2603.03406)
- **Less context can be better**: 2K-token structured diff summary outperforms 2.5K full-context prompt across all models (SWE-PRBench)
- **Frontier models catch only 15-31%** of human-flagged issues (SWE-PRBench)
- **Three agents (Main + Reviewer + Critic) outperform six agents** when disagreement is structured (Adversarial Review paper)
- **Temperature 0.2** is the deliberate choice for review (Qodo) -- precision over creativity
- **Randomized diff ordering** exploits positional bias for broader coverage (Cursor V1)
- **Majority voting** (>=2/N passes must flag) filters hallucinated findings (Cursor V1)</result>

<result>I now have all the data needed for a comprehensive report. Here is the full architecture analysis.

---

## Sweep AI Code Review Architecture -- Deep Dive

### Repository

**GitHub**: [sweepai/sweep](https://github.com/sweepai/sweep) (7.7k stars, 462 forks, 10,258 commits). Python 44.8%, Jupyter 47.7%, TypeScript 6.6%. The current README is gutted to a 5-line redirect because the team pivoted to a JetBrains plugin, but the full GitHub App codebase remains intact and readable.

---

### Integration Method: GitHub App + FastAPI Webhook

Sweep runs as a **GitHub App** receiving webhooks via a **FastAPI** server (`sweepai/api.py`). The single POST endpoint at `/` validates GitHub HMAC signatures (`validate_signature`), then routes events via Python pattern matching:

- `"pull_request", "opened"` -- triggers PR review
- `"pull_request", "labeled"` -- Sweep label triggers review
- `"issues", "opened"` -- ticket-to-PR pipeline
- `"issue_comment", "created/edited"` -- comment handling
- `"check_run", "completed"` -- CI failure detection

Reviews are dispatched to background threads: `threading.Thread(target=run_review_pr)`. Comment processing uses a `SafePriorityQueue` to serialize concurrent comments on the same PR.

**Self-hosting** is supported via Docker Compose. Requires `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PEM`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `COHERE_API_KEY` as environment variables. The container exposes port 8080.

---

### Multi-Model Approach

Sweep uses a **multi-provider, single-model-per-task** strategy -- not multiple models competing on the same task:

**Primary review model**: `claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620` (hardcoded as `CLAUDE_MODEL` in `sweepai/core/review_utils.py`, line 399). Every review-related LLM call uses this.

**Fallback routing** in `chat_anthropic()`:
- Default: Anthropic API (direct or via AWS Bedrock)
- If no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: falls back to `gpt-4o` via OpenAI
- Azure OpenAI support via `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT` env vars
- Multi-region config supported via `MULTI_REGION_CONFIG` (newline-delimited regions)

**Other models used elsewhere**:
- `claude-3-opus-20240229` in `sweep_bot.py` for issue-to-PR generation
- `claude-3-haiku-20240307` for lightweight tasks (commit messages in `pull_request_bot.py`)
- OpenAI embeddings for vector search/similarity

**Temperature**: `0.1` globally (set as `default_temperature`), used consistently across all review calls.

---

### Review Pipeline Architecture (5 Stages + Majority Vote)

The core review function is `group_vote_review_pr()` in `sweepai/core/review_utils.py`. This is the most architecturally significant piece:

#### Stage 0: Majority Vote Wrapper (5 parallel runs)

The function runs the **entire review pipeline 5 times in parallel** (`GROUP_SIZE = 5`) using Python `multiprocessing.Pool(processes=5)`. Each run gets a different `seed` value (0-4) for temperature-based variation. Results are then clustered and voted on.

**Consensus mechanism**: After all 5 runs complete:
1. Every issue from all runs is embedded into a 512-dim vector via `embed_text_array()`
2. **DBSCAN clustering** (`eps=0.375, min_samples=2`) groups semantically similar issues
3. Only clusters with **>= 4 occurrences** (`LABEL_THRESHOLD = 4`) out of 5 runs become "confirmed issues"
4. Clusters with exactly 3 occurrences become "potential issues"
5. The representative issue for each cluster is selected by highest cosine similarity to all other cluster members (`get_group_voted_best_issue_index()`)
6. Noise labels (`-1`) are discarded

This is a genuine ensemble approach -- the same model run 5 times with different seeds, then DBSCAN + embedding-based deduplication to filter signal from noise.

#### Stage 1: Initial Code Analysis (`review_code_changes_by_file`)

- System prompt: "careful and smart tech lead that wants to avoid production issues"
- Analyzes diffs line-by-line with structured XML output
- Parallel: checks directory-hierarchy `SWEEP.md` files for custom rules (cascading from subdirectory to root)
- For special rules, uses a separate system prompt: "tech lead checking against custom rules"

#### Stage 2: Edge Case Detection (Self-Q&A)

Two-pass self-interrogation:
1. **Question creation** (system prompt: "careful and smart tech lead"): generates exhaustive questions about concurrency issues, variable mutation, ordering bugs. Questions are phrased so "Yes" = there is a problem.
2. **Question answering** (separate system prompt): independently answers the generated questions with code evidence, then identifies issues from affirmative answers.

#### Stage 3: Critical Review (`review_code_issues_by_file`)

- System prompt: "busy tech manager responsible for reviewing PRs"
- Re-evaluates all issues from Stages 1-2 using a **3-question severity assessment** per issue
- Incorporates existing PR comment threads to avoid duplicate findings
- Checks if issues were already raised in previous reviews
- Filters to only "severe issues" that would prevent merge

#### Stage 4: Function Deduplication

- Identifies newly created utility functions in patches
- Uses embedding-based search against the full codebase to find existing functions with identical purpose
- Flags redundant function definitions as issues

#### Stage 5: Severity Sorting

- All surviving issues are ranked by an LLM-based severity sort
- Capped at `MAX_ISSUE_AMOUNT = 10` final issues

---

### Reviewer Personas (System Prompts)

Sweep uses **8 distinct system prompt personas**, each for a specific review sub-task:

| Persona | Role | Used In |
|---------|------|---------|
| "careful and smart tech lead" | Initial code analysis | Stage 1 main review |
| "busy tech manager" | Severity filtering | Stage 3 critical review |
| "tech lead checking rules" | Custom rule validation | SWEEP.md rule checking |
| "tech lead asking questions" | Edge case question creation | Stage 2 Q&A |
| "tech lead answering questions" | Edge case validation | Stage 2 Q&A |
| "expert programmer with keen eye" | Function identification | Stage 4 |
| "proficient programmer" | Duplicate function detection | Stage 4 |
| "talented software engineer" | PR summarization | Summary generation |
| "helpful detail-oriented engineer" | Issue severity sorting | Stage 5 |

---

### Output Format and Severity Classification

**No formal severity enum exists.** The dataclass `CodeReviewIssue` has only 3 fields:
```python
@dataclass
class CodeReviewIssue:
    file_name: str
    issue_description: str
    line_number: str
```

Severity is implicit in the pipeline structure:
- Issues surviving all 5 parallel runs (DBSCAN threshold >= 4) = **confirmed issues**
- Issues at threshold - 1 (exactly 3 of 5 runs) = **potential issues**
- Everything else = discarded

All LLM outputs use **structured XML tags** (not JSON):
```xml
<issues>
  <issue>
    <issue_description>...</issue_description>
    <file_name>...</file_name>
    <line_number>...</line_number>
  </issue>
</issues>
```

Final output is posted as a **GitHub PR comment** with markdown formatting, linking each issue to the specific file blob URL and diff URL with line anchors.

---

### Context Window Management

- **Token budget**: ~120k tokens (`MAX_CHAR_BUDGET = 120000 * 3.5 chars`)
- **Progressive truncation** when over budget:
  1. Full source with annotations
  2. `smart_prune_file_based_on_patches()` -- keeps only 10 lines of context around each patch
  3. Drop annotations
  4. Skip file entirely
- **Diff length cap**: 1000 lines max per file (`MAX_DIFF_LENGTH`)
- Files are clustered by DBSCAN on patch embeddings before review, so related files are reviewed together

---

### Custom Rules System (SWEEP.md)

Users place `SWEEP.md` files at any directory level. The system walks from the changed file's directory up to repo root, collecting all `SWEEP.md` files. Rules cascade -- deeper rules augment, not replace, parent rules. The prompt includes rule examples verbatim and instructs the model to check each rule against each code change independently.

---

### Key Architectural Decisions

1. **XML over JSON for LLM output**: All structured outputs use XML tags, parsed with regex. No Pydantic/JSON schema validation on LLM output.
2. **Embedding-based consensus instead of simple majority vote**: DBSCAN clustering on issue embeddings rather than string matching, which handles paraphrased duplicates.
3. **Self-Q&A pattern for edge cases**: The model generates questions, then a fresh context answers them -- forcing systematic consideration of concurrency bugs, mutation issues, etc.
4. **No inline PR review comments**: Issues are posted as a single PR comment with links, not as GitHub review comments on specific lines (though `create_review_comments_for_code_issues` exists in the codebase).
5. **Annotation layer**: Diffs are pre-annotated by Claude 3 Sonnet before review, giving the reviewer model richer context about what each change does.
6. **File caching**: `@file_cache()` decorator on `get_pr_changes` and `call_openai` to avoid redundant API calls.

---

### Open Source Status

The full codebase is open source under the `sweepai/sweep` repo. All prompt templates, review logic, and orchestration code are readable. The team has since pivoted focus to a JetBrains plugin (closed source), but the GitHub App code remains intact on the `main` branch.

input.prompt:
Research how to build a real-time web dashboard for viewing Claude Code workflow progress. The context:

Claude Code has a `/workflows` TUI view that shows inflight workflow progress, but it's hard to read in the terminal. We want a web-based alternative that shows:

1. **Inflight workflow status** — which agents are running, which completed, which failed
2. **Phase progress** — which phase (Topology, Setup, Act, Merge, Cleanup) is active
3. **Agent tree** — nested view of agents with labels, status, duration
4. **Log stream** — `log()` messages in real time
5. **Token usage** — running total of tokens consumed

Research these approaches:

### Option A: Tail the workflow transcript JSONL
- Claude Code writes workflow transcripts to `.claude/projects/*/subagents/workflows/` as JSONL files
- A lightweight server could tail these files and serve SSE/WebSocket events to a browser
- What format are these JSONL files in? What fields do they contain?

### Option B: Claude Code's built-in mechanisms
- Does Claude Code have any API or hook for workflow progress events?
- Can we use the Monitor tool or any other mechanism to stream events?
- Is there a way to intercept workflow progress programmatically?

### Option C: Custom progress file
- Our workflow script could write a progress JSON file (e.g., `.datum/runs/<runId>/progress.json`)
- `log()` calls and agent completions update this file
- A simple HTTP server serves it with auto-refresh

### Option D: Existing tools
- Are there any existing workflow visualization tools that can consume JSONL?
- Something like Grafana, or a simpler purpose-built tool?

### Technical constraints:
- Must work on macOS
- Should be a single-file HTML or minimal server (no heavy frameworks)
- Real-time updates (SSE or polling, not manual refresh)
- Should look good — dark theme, monospace, progress bars

For each option, assess feasibility and provide a concrete implementation sketch. Which is the simplest to build that gives 80% of the value?

Report concisely — bullet points, not essays. Max 500 words.

## Sourcery.ai Code Review Architecture -- Research Report

### Product URLs and Repos

- **Product site**: https://www.sourcery.ai/
- **Documentation**: https://docs.sourcery.ai/
- **Main GitHub repo**: https://github.com/sourcery-ai/sourcery (MIT license, 1.8k stars, Python -- but the core review engine is proprietary SaaS; the repo is essentially the client/CLI wrapper)
- **GitHub org**: https://github.com/sourcery-ai (25 repos total)

**Open source components:**

| Repo | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `sourcery` | CLI client + GitHub App shell (MIT) |
| `sourcery-vscode` | VS Code extension (TypeScript, MIT) |
| `sourcery-analytics` | Standalone Python code quality metrics CLI (Python, MIT) -- measures complexity, method length, working memory, cognitive complexity |
| `sourcery-rules` | Curated YAML rule sets (google-python-style-guide, remove-debugging-statements, etc.) |
| `sourcery-rules-generator` | Experimental tool that generates architecture/dependency rules from a codebase |
| `action` | GitHub Action wrapper (MIT) |
| `tree-sitter-python`, `tree-sitter-java` | Forked tree-sitter grammars -- confirms they use tree-sitter for AST parsing in the static analysis engine |
| `lsp4intellij` | Fork of LSP library for JetBrains -- their IDE integration uses Language Server Protocol |

The review engine itself (the LLM pipeline, the static analysis engine, the validation system) is **closed source / proprietary SaaS**.

---

### Integration Methods

1. **GitHub App** -- Installs at the org/repo level. Automatically reviews PRs marked ready. Manual trigger via `@sourcery-ai review` comment. Also supports `@sourcery-ai summary`, `@sourcery-ai guide`, `@sourcery-ai title`, `@sourcery-ai dismiss`, `@sourcery-ai resolve`, `@sourcery-ai issue` (converts a review comment into a GitHub Issue).
2. **GitLab integration** -- Same PR review flow, including self-hosted GitLab.
3. **IDE plugins** -- VS Code, JetBrains (PyCharm), Cursor, Sublime, Vim. Uses LSP. Reviews current file, uncommitted changes, or branch diff. Hover-to-see-comment, one-click apply fix.
4. **GitHub Action** (`sourcery-ai/action@v1`) -- CI integration. Parameters: `token`, `target`, `check` (fail CI on issues), `fix` (auto-apply fixes in-place), `config` (path to .sourcery.yaml), `diff_ref` (review only changed lines vs a base SHA).
5. **Vercel Marketplace** -- Native integration for Vercel deployments.
6. **Pre-commit hook** -- Via PyPI package.

---

### Review Pipeline Architecture (the 7-step pipeline)

This is the most architecturally significant finding, from their blog post "Tackling Complex Tasks with LLMs":

1. **Split into atomic chunks** -- PR diff is broken into per-function/per-class fragments. They explicitly avoid sending full-file or full-repo context because "increasing the size of the context provided to an LLM has diminishing returns and, at a certain point, seems to actually harm the accuracy."

2. **Deterministic heuristic pre-filter** -- Eliminates chunks unlikely to need review (import-only changes, small modifications, non-code changes). This saves ~5000+ tokens per review by avoiding LLM calls on irrelevant diffs.

3. **Context expansion** -- Expands surviving diff hunks from raw diff into before/after code views (full function bodies, not just changed lines).

4. **LLM analysis with chain-of-thought** -- First LLM pass generates analysis with reasoning. Includes initial filtering (the LLM itself classifies whether its finding is relevant).

5. **LLM structured response generation** -- Second LLM pass formats the analysis into developer-facing feedback (separate from the reasoning step).

6. **Second LLM filter (validator)** -- A separate LLM instance evaluates each generated comment against 4 critical validators (see below). Comments failing validation are discarded.

7. **Post-processing** -- Final formatting, deduplication, assembly into the review output.

**Efficiency claim**: 77% reduction in token usage vs single-LLM approach, 80%+ reduction in false positives through the secondary filter.

---

### Multi-Model Approach

**Dual-LLM provider**: Sourcery sends code to **both OpenAI and Anthropic** models. The DeepWiki analysis describes this as "redundancy and enhanced analysis capabilities." The exact models are not disclosed, but they confirmed using both providers.

**Multi-reviewer personas**: Multiple specialized AI reviewers run in parallel on the same diff, each with a different focus:
- **General code quality** reviewer
- **Security** reviewer (SAST-style)
- **Complexity** reviewer -- focuses on whether changes introduce unnecessary complexity
- **Documentation** reviewer
- **Testing** reviewer
- **Custom review instructions** (user-defined via dashboard)

This is a genuine multi-agent architecture -- different prompt personas analyzing the same code from different angles, not a single reviewer with a big prompt.

---

### Prompting Strategy

Sourcery has published three key blog posts revealing their prompting approach:

**1. Panel-of-Experts (Tree-of-Thought variant)**
From `/blog/panel-of-experts`. System prompt creates three named experts (Alice, Bob, Charles) who:
- Each write one step of thinking, then share with the group
- Challenge each other's reasoning
- If any expert realizes they're wrong, they leave
- Consensus emerges through deliberation
- Output is structured JSON

Example system prompt: *"You are a panel of three experts on code documentation - Alice, Bob and Charles. When given a diff containing code changes, your task is to determine any updates required to the docstrings"*

**Performance**: Reduced error rate from ~40% (Chain-of-Thought) to ~20%. Cost: 2x token usage due to deliberation.

**2. Classification-based filtering (not negative prompting)**
From `/blog/dont-tell-me-what-not-to-do`. Key finding: **negative prompting backfires** -- telling the LLM "don't do X" makes it more likely to do X. Their solution: ask the LLM to classify its own output with a boolean metadata field (e.g., `has_existing_docstring: true/false`), then filter in post-processing. This pattern is "applied to various different aspects" of their review process.

**3. Multi-pass over single-pass**
From `/blog/tackling-complex-tasks-with-llms`. Rather than one big prompt with full context, they use sequential LLM calls with smaller focused context, plus deterministic pre-filtering between steps.

---

### Comment Validation System (the 4-check validator)

From `/blog/improving-llm-responses`. After generating review comments, a **separate LLM validator** evaluates each comment against 7 criteria, of which 4 proved critical:

1. **Valid to the code** -- Is the comment factually correct about what the code does?
2. **Actionable** -- Can the developer do something concrete with this feedback?
3. **Specific** -- Is this specific to this code, or generic advice that could apply anywhere?
4. **Valuable to the author** -- Would the developer actually benefit from seeing this?

Three additional criteria exist but had less impact: factually correct, contextually correct, accounts for other PR changes.

**Before validation**: ~40% usefulness rate. **After 4-check validation**: ~60% usefulness rate.

**Failed approaches they tried first**: prompt expansion ("be useful"), chain-of-reasoning, self-filtering (same LLM judging its own output -- "LLMs seem pretty reluctant to say that their own creation isn't useful"), single alternative validator.

---

### Output Format and Review Structure

Each PR review contains these sections (all toggleable via dashboard):

1. **PR Summary** (enabled by default) -- "Summary by Sourcery" header, followed by categorized bullet points (e.g., "Bug Fixes:", "Documentation:", "Enhancement:")
2. **Review Guide** (enabled by default) -- "Reviewer's Guide by Sourcery" with change summary, file-level changes table, and optionally class/sequence diagrams
3. **Mermaid Diagrams** (enabled by default) -- Auto-generated for complex changes
4. **AI Review Comments** (enabled by default) -- Inline line-by-line comments on the PR diff
5. **Tips and Commands** (enabled by default) -- Interaction guide
6. **PR Approvals** (disabled by default) -- Can auto-approve PRs

Inline comments support: thumbs up/down reactions (used to train future reviews), reply threads (Sourcery responds to questions), `@sourcery-ai issue` to convert a comment to a GitHub Issue.

---

### Severity / Classification System

Sourcery does **not** use a formal severity taxonomy (Critical/High/Medium/Low) on individual comments. Instead, they use:

**Rule types** (for the static analysis engine):
- `refactoring` -- Code transformation suggestions
- `suggestion` -- Improvement recommendations
- `comment` -- Informational notes

**Comment types** (for LLM-generated comments, visible in their test suite):
- Comments are internally classified by type (e.g., "issue", "testing", "security") -- their unit tests verify comment type classification rather than exact wording.

**Code quality metrics** (for the static analysis engine):
- Quality Score: 0-100% blended metric
- Complexity: Cognitive complexity (SonarSource methodology)
- Method Length: AST node count
- Working Memory: Max variables simultaneously in scope (based on cognitive science, 5-9 item limit)
- `quality_threshold` configurable in `.sourcery.yaml` (default: 25.0)

**Security scanning severity**: Added in Dec 2025 -- SAST, SCA (powered by Trivy), secrets detection, IaC scanning, license scanning. These do have severity rankings and can create blocking check statuses on PRs.

---

### Configuration System

`.sourcery.yaml` at project root:

```yaml
ignore:
  - test_*.py
  - data/*

rule_settings:
  enable: [default]
  disable: []
  rule_types:
    - refactoring
    - suggestion
    - comment
  python_version: '3.9'

rules:
  - id: my-custom-rule
    description: What it checks
    pattern: source_code_pattern_with_${captures}
    replacement: fixed_code_with_${captures}
    tags: [tag1, tag2]
    paths:
      include: [src/**/*.py]
      exclude: [tests/**]
    tests:
      - match: code_snippet
        expect: expected_output
      - no-match: code_snippet

rule_tags:
  my-tag:
    - rule-id-1
    - rule-id-2

metrics:
  quality_threshold: 25.0

clone_detection:
  min_lines: 3
  min_duplicates: 2
  identical_clones_only: false
```

Custom review rules are also configurable via the Sourcery Dashboard (web UI), where you can:
- Set natural language review instructions (with path pattern scoping via globs)
- Toggle each review section on/off
- Set preferred review language
- Enable/disable specific static analysis rules for Python and JavaScript

---

### Testing Strategy for LLM Output

From `/blog/unit-testing-llm-output`:
- They call **real LLMs in tests** (no mocking) because they can't predict response variation
- Assert on **comment type classification** (e.g., "this should be a security comment"), not exact wording
- Use **keyword/theme scanning** for content relevance
- Use **exclusion checks** (e.g., "praise comments must not appear")
- CI pass threshold: **95%** -- they accept 5% flakiness from LLM non-determinism
- They validate file location and line numbers are correct, not the comment text

---

### Key Architectural Differentiators

1. **Primarily file-scoped analysis** -- they explicitly do not do cross-file dependency analysis (a known limitation called out in the Qodo comparison)
2. **Hybrid static + LLM** -- the static analysis engine (using tree-sitter for AST) handles deterministic rules; LLMs handle contextual/semantic analysis
3. **Post-generation filtering over prompt engineering** -- their key insight is that it's more effective to generate-then-filter than to craft perfect prompts
4. **Classification metadata on every LLM output** -- rather than behavioral constraints, they ask LLMs to self-classify, then filter programmatically
5. **300+ built-in Python rules, expanding JavaScript** -- deep Python-first heritage

## Adversarial Review Subagents: Industry Patterns

### 1. Your Local Claude Code Adversarial Reviewer

**Path:** `/Users/samfakhreddine/.agents/skills/adversarial-reviewer/SKILL.md`

- **Prompt framing:** Explicitly hostile -- "guilty until proven innocent," "no compliments, only bugs," silence means approval
- **Tool restrictions:** None specified; standard read-only analysis
- **Output format:** Each bug includes title, file:line, category, severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), trigger scenario (concrete inputs that break it), and minimal fix
- **Checklist:** 7 categories -- logic errors, edge cases, error handling, state/concurrency, security, data integrity, resource management
- **Architecture:** Single-agent, no sub-agents, no model/temperature override
- **What it explicitly is NOT:** style review, feature review, test review, or compliment sandwich

Your broader Claude Code review ecosystem includes 11 review-adjacent skills. The most architecturally interesting is **wp-audit** (whitepaper audit), which orchestrates 7 parallel specialist agents + a synthesis agent + Python post-processing with Pydantic schema validation -- the most sophisticated multi-agent review pattern in your local setup.

---

### 2. Production Code Review Tools

#### PR-Agent (Qodo, open source)
- **Prompts:** TOML + Jinja2 templates in `pr_agent/settings/`. Not adversarial; professional tone. Default mode `focus_only_on_problems=true` restricts output to Security/Critical Bug/General (closest thing to adversarial)
- **Output:** YAML, Pydantic-validated. Each suggestion gets a 0-10 self-reflection score
- **Self-validation:** Two-pass -- primary LLM generates suggestions, second call scores them. Auto-zero categories: docstrings, type hints, comments, unused imports
- **Score caps:** Verification-only suggestions capped at 7; error handling capped at 8
- **Model:** User-configurable, sequential fallback. Same model for both passes
- **No adversarial mode.** No multi-perspective review. No competing agents.

#### CodeRabbit (closed source, most sophisticated)
- **8-stage pipeline:** Webhook -> code graph -> context assembly -> 50+ static analyzers -> AI exploration scripts -> 3-pass LLM review -> verification agent -> output
- **Multi-model:** Cheap model (Nemotron) for triage/classification, frontier model (GPT-5/Claude Opus 4) for line review
- **Proposer-validator, not adversarial:** Verification agent generates shell/Python scripts to confirm findings against actual code. Filters hallucinations. Not a competing perspective
- **Context ratio:** 1:1 code-to-context; 80-90% of tokens spent on context, not generation
- **Severity:** Critical/Major/Minor/Trivial/Info. Separates "Potential Issue" from "Refactor Suggestion" from "Nitpick"
- **Accuracy:** 51.2% F1 (highest of 10 tools benchmarked). ~2 false positives per review

#### GitHub Copilot Code Review
- **Architecture:** Agentic tool-calling on GitHub Actions runners. Reads related files, traces imports, explores directory structure before reviewing
- **Two effort levels:** Low (standard model, fast) and Medium (routes to "higher-reasoning models")
- **Comment-only:** Never approves or requests changes. Does not count toward required approvals
- **Severity:** High/Medium/Low. Suggestions rendered as committable GitHub suggestion blocks
- **No adversarial mode.** Exploration-first, not critique-first

#### Qodo Merge 2.0 (February 2026)
- **Parallel specialized agents:** Bug detection, security analysis, code quality, test coverage -- each runs independently
- **Cross-repo context:** Pulls from past PRs and prior review decisions
- **Highest benchmark F1:** 60.1% among 8 tested tools for finding real defects
- **Built on PR-Agent** open-source engine

---

### 3. Academic / Research Patterns

#### Generator-Critic (most mature pattern)
- **CTRL (ICML 2025):** Critic trained via RL independently from generator. Can pair with any generator at test time. Binary reward (correct/incorrect judgment). 106% relative improvement in Pass@1 via iterative critique-revision loops. Model: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B. [arXiv:2502.03492](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03492)
- **Critique-Coder (2025):** Hybrid training -- 80% standard RL + 20% critique RL. Critique capability manifests as longer reasoning traces, not a separate post-hoc step. 20% CRL is the sweet spot; too much biases toward evaluation over generation. [arXiv:2509.22824](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22824)
- **AgentCoder (2024):** Three agents -- Programmer, Test Designer, Test Executor. Communication is structured (test results and error messages), not open-ended chat. Structured feedback is critical to prevent noise. [arXiv:2312.13010](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13010)

#### Debate Pattern (promising but dangerous)
- **Standard architecture:** N agents answer independently, then iteratively refine after seeing others' responses. Temperature 1.0 across all agents. Terminated via adaptive stability detection (Beta-Binomial + KS statistic)
- **Requirements Engineering Debate:** Functional Debater + Non-Functional Debater + Judge. F1 improved from 0.726 to 0.835, but at **9.5x token cost**

Blue team distills red findings into constitutional rules + dynamic sandbox testing (Docker execution to verify vulnerabilities actually manifest). 12.7% F1 improvement. - Framing a code change as "bug-free" reduces vulnerability detection by **16-93%**
- GPT-4o-mini drops from 97.2% to 3.6% detection when told the code is safe
- Researchers crafted PRs that reintroduce known CVEs framed as "security improvements" -- Copilot and Claude Code both fell for them

- **Architectural implication:** Security-focused review agents should operate on sanitized code only, separate from metadata interpretation

#### Simple Outperforms Complex for Code Judgment (AXIOM, December 2025)
- LLM judges have a "pronounced bias toward defect detection" -- misclassify non-defective code as defective
- **Scoring consistency inversely correlates with procedural complexity** -- complex agentic frameworks suffer more from variance
- Simple single-pass metrics outperform complex agentic workflows for code judgment
- [arXiv:2512.20159](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20159)

#### False Positive Handling (ranked by effectiveness)
1. **Dynamic sandbox verification** (execute suspicious code to confirm) -- BlueCodeAgent
2. **Self-consistency voting** (5 independent analyses, majority vote) -- 85%+ false positive elimination
3. **Precision calibration** (set threshold to 50% precision, trade recall for trust) -- Google
4. **Pre-debate triage** (only trigger expensive review when confidence is low) -- iMAD
5. **Structured context slicing** (give reviewer only relevant code paths, not entire files)

#### Temperature and Model Selection
- No published system recommends different temperatures for generator vs. reviewer
- Debate systems uniformly use temperature 1.0 for diversity
- Model selection is generally same-tier (no "use a cheaper model for review")
- Strongest isolation: train the critic as a separate model entirely (CTRL)

## Greptile Code Review Agent Architecture -- Research Report

### Product URLs

- **Product**: https://www.greptile.com
- **Docs**: https://www.greptile.com/docs (new site) and https://docs.greptile.com (older API docs)
- **GitHub Org**: https://github.com/greptileai (46 repos, core engine is closed source)
- **Open Source Repos**:
  - `greptileai/skills` -- MIT-licensed agent skills (`check-pr`, `greploop`) for Claude Code / agent integrations
  - `greptileai/cli` -- thin shell/Node.js installer for the CLI binary (the CLI itself is a prebuilt JS bundle)
